audit.why: EVEN 6/10 at 50.7% over 1278 games is right as an overall verdict, but the lane shape is lopsided: Riven owns only Level 1 and Camille owns levels 2 through first item.
audit.corrected: Rating kept; the per-stage sides rebuilt (point 3).

audit.whatIsWrong: Every one of the seven level-chart rows disagreed with the packet chart and with this page's own why text — the page gave Riven levels 2, 3, first item and two items while whys[1], whys[2], whys[5] and whys[6] say Camille wins those or that the duel is a coin flip.
audit.why: packet.levelChart is [Riven, Camille, Camille, Camille, Camille, Camille, Skill] and matches whys[0..6] row for row. Camille's spikes are Level 2 (Tactical Sweep), Level 6 (The Hextech Ultimatum, 140s) and Trinity Force.
audit.corrected: All seven rows flipped as matched full/content pairs, with the generic phases whys rewritten to justify the new sides and to carry Hookshot's 16s rank-1 cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page attributes true damage to Tactical Sweep (W) in whys[1], early, wants.foe[1] and wants.you[2].
audit.why: Riot data puts trueDamage on Precision Protocol (Q, 9s at rank 1) — the recast that hits far harder if she delays between the two attacks. Tactical Sweep (W, 15s) is a delayed cone whose outer half slows, deals extra damage and HEALS her. Telling a player to fear true damage from the wrong ability makes them dodge the wrong thing and stand in the half that funds her sustain.
audit.corrected: True damage moved to Precision Protocol's delayed recast; Tactical Sweep restated as the outer-cone heal. Precision Protocol is also an auto-attack reset, so the wind-up is the step-back cue.

audit.whatIsWrong: mid told you to fight 'when Hookshot is visibly on cooldown' without saying how long that is.
audit.why: Hookshot is 16/15/14/13/12 — a 16-second window at rank 1 in which she has neither engage nor escape. That number is the whole gameplan.
audit.corrected: mid and phases[3].why now carry the 16s figure.

audit.why: Early Executioner's Calling is correct here — Tactical Sweep's outer half heals her off every trade she lands.

edits.before: Your Q resets win level 1 if you weave autos between casts. Identify how Camille contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Runic Blade weaving off Broken Wings is your one early edge — she has no Tactical Sweep yet, so poke her and take wave priority now.

edits.before: E shield lets you take a trade and refund his answer. Only take the trade when Camille's Hookshot is down.
edits.after: Her damage arrives at 2 and Precision Protocol's delayed recast is true damage — refuse every prolonged trade here.

edits.before: Camille hits Level 2 and Tactical Sweep's true-damage second hit comes online — she now wins any prolonged trade and her Hookshot gives her an escape you cannot match.
edits.after: At Level 2 her damage stacks up: Precision Protocol's delayed recast is the true damage, Tactical Sweep's outer cone heals her back, and Hookshot escapes whatever you start.

edits.before: At Level 1 you actually have a narrow edge — use your Q chain to weave Runic Blade procs onto her before she levels W. The moment she hits Level 2 and Tactical Sweep is live, respect the lane: her second-hit cone deals true damage and heals her, and it will eat through your E Valor shield if she catches you flat-footed. Do not fight through her W second hit under any circumstances — the heal and true damage flip the trade hard against you.
edits.after: At Level 1 you actually have a narrow edge — use your Q chain to weave Runic Blade procs onto her before she levels W. The moment she hits Level 2, respect the lane: the true damage is on Precision Protocol's delayed recast, and Tactical Sweep's outer half slows you and heals her, refunding whatever you chipped off. Never stand in the outer cone and never eat a delayed Q recast — together they flip the trade hard against you.

edits.before: Camille owns this stretch. Her E Hookshot into wall-stun followed by the full Q true damage proc and W is one of the cleanest all-in patterns in the game, and she can reset Hookshot off the wall to escape. Your only real window is when Hookshot is visibly on cooldown — the instant it goes down, close the gap with your own E Valor, land W Ki Burst before she can dash again, and burn your full Q chain. If her E is up, do not step into range; she will simply engage on her terms and isolate you.
edits.after: Camille owns this stretch. Her E Hookshot into wall-stun followed by the delayed Precision Protocol recast is one of the cleanest all-in patterns in the game, and she can jump off the wall again to escape. Your only real window is the 16 seconds after Hookshot goes down at rank 1 — close with your own E Valor, land Ki Burst before she can dash again, and burn the full Q chain. If her E is up, do not step into range; she engages on her terms and isolates you.

edits.before: Use W Tactical Sweep second hit true damage to shred through your E shield mid-trade
edits.after: Delay the Precision Protocol recast so the empowered true-damage hit lands through your shield

edits.after: Force short Q-auto-weave trades at Level 1, before Tactical Sweep gives her outer-cone healing

notes: The whole level chart was inverted against both the packet and its own whys — 7 matched pairs proposed as one group. The packet flagged 'Hextech Ultimatum' and 'Tactical Sweep's' as suspect names: both are FALSE POSITIVES (the real names are The Hextech Ultimatum and Tactical Sweep). The genuine error was which ability carries true damage. NOT WRITTEN, deliberately: the missing-interactions file claims The Hextech Ultimatum is a channel your Ki Burst cancels outright, and the kit carries an 'untargetable' flag on it. Riot's own description says only that she dashes to the target and anchors them — neither claim is supported by the text and I could not verify them, so no such advice was added. See unverified.
